items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: Well then after a while in comes my piano player, Tom Zimmerman

ctx.x: You know? Well then after a while in comes my piano player, Tom Zimmerman, one of the greatest, I can't tell you how great he was and couldn't read a note as big as a customer. When he played he was Frankie Call and another Frankie Call. My idea of a rhythm piano player, I mean clean playing, was Frankie Call. Did you ever hear Frankie Call? Sure. Didn't he have a touch? Beautiful. And melodic too.

items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: I said, Tom, what's the title of the Grand March? It's beautiful. He said, title? He said, I made it up.

ctx.x: I used the guitar at the Beverly Gardens and I used them on Biloxi because he didn't play banjo. Uh-huh. But he played so much guitar. You know what I mean? They played. They loved it and they played. That's all. But the original was just five men without any bass. And I always thought that I should have always had a bass instead of the banjo.
